assertion: Restore valid previous-day source archive into new empty volume; success after compatibility/origin/attestation; refuse restore on occupied target regardless of age.
environment: Disposable GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.15.2, real Docker daemon and pinned Python OCI image.
initial_state: An encrypted and signed SQLite fixture archive dated the previous day, a valid signed procedure attestation, and an unused Docker volume name.
scenario: Restore a previous-day Docker volume archive to a new empty volume through the offline Rescue CLI.
fault_injection: Retry with the occupied volume name; test the occupied target independently after the successful write.
observation: The CLI returned RESTORE_WRITTEN. A read-only Docker mount confirmed file ownership, mode, SQLite integrity and restored application data. The second CLI attempt returned RESTORE_DOCKER_TARGET_EXISTS; target checks returned RESTORE_TARGET_OCCUPIED.
reviewer: Codex verified the fresh CI checkout and result; project Owner accepted the earlier laboratory run on 2026-11-10 as recorded in README.
limitations: The restore job uses source code on the same tested tree as the separate signed development build.
Offline terminal and Owner input are fixtures; generated test credentials and attestation are used.
Scope is the disposable Docker resource restore; Controller disaster recovery and MVP release have separate criteria.
